chapter_title: DBMS UNIT - I: Database System Concepts, ER Model & Relational Design

questions.stem: Why does a relational Natural Join (R ⋈ S) produce an output schema with degree strictly less than Deg(R) + Deg(S) when shared attribute names exist?

options.A: Because Natural Join projects out duplicate join attribute columns after equating them
options.B: Because the query optimizer compresses null-valued attributes into binary masks
options.C: Because relational engines discard non-primary key attributes from the right table
options.D: Because Natural Join computes the Cartesian product only on foreign key columns

questions.explanation: Natural Join is algebraically defined as a Cartesian product followed by selection on equality of all shared attributes, followed by projection that retains only one copy of each shared attribute.

questions.stem: In the Three-Schema Architecture, why is Logical Data Independence significantly harder to achieve than Physical Data Independence?

options.A: Because physical disk storage devices evolve faster than application code
options.B: Because the SQL standard does not support external view definitions
options.C: Because altering conceptual schemas often changes the semantic structure of tables, making view reconstruction and view updatability difficult or impossible
options.D: Because operating system file managers prohibit column additions on live databases

questions.explanation: Physical independence only requires updating internal pointers/indexes. Logical independence requires altering table structures (splitting, restructuring) while preserving external views, which is constrained by view updatability and complex semantic mappings.

questions.stem: When mapping a 1:1 relationship between entity set A and entity set B where A has Total Participation and B has Partial Participation, where should the foreign key be placed to minimize NULL values?

options.A: In relation B, declared with a NOT NULL constraint
options.B: In relation A, declared with a NOT NULL and UNIQUE constraint
options.C: In a separate associative table containing both primary keys
options.D: In both relations simultaneously to enforce bidirectional referential integrity

questions.explanation: Placing the foreign key in table A (total participation) ensures every row in A references a B instance, allowing a `NOT NULL` constraint and completely eliminating null foreign keys.

questions.stem: What critical anomaly occurs if the Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) protocol is violated by writing a modified buffer pool page to disk before its corresponding transaction log record is persisted?

options.A: The query optimizer will select a sub-optimal sequential scan plan
options.B: The buffer manager will trigger a deadlock in the concurrency control manager
options.C: The database catalog will lose track of primary key constraints
options.D: A system crash can leave uncommitted dirty data on disk with no log record to UNDO the changes, permanently violating Atomicity

questions.explanation: WAL mandates that log records must reach non-volatile disk before dirty data pages are flushed. If violated, a crash leaves uncommitted updates on disk without undo records, violating atomicity.

questions.stem: Consider a relation R(A, B, C, D) with candidate keys {A, B} and {A, C}. Which of the following attribute sets is NOT a super key of R?
questions.explanation: Any superset of a candidate key is a super key. {A, B, D} contains {A, B}; {A, C} is a candidate key; {A, B, C, D} contains both. {B, C, D} contains neither {A, B} nor {A, C}, so it is not a super key.

questions.stem: Which of the following scenarios illustrates a violation of Referential Integrity during a database modification?

options.A: Inserting a new department row into the Department table with a unique Dept_ID
options.B: Deleting a child row from an associative table
options.C: Updating an employee's salary to a value within the allowable domain
options.D: Inserting an employee row into the Employee table with a Dept_ID value that does not exist in the Department table

questions.explanation: Referential integrity requires foreign key values to match an existing primary key in the referenced table. Inserting an employee with a non-existent Dept_ID creates an orphan record, violating referential integrity.

questions.stem: What is the result of evaluating the Relational Algebra expression R - (R - S) when R and S are union-compatible relations?

options.B: R ∩ S (Set Intersection of R and S)

questions.explanation: $R - S$ contains tuples in $R$ but not in $S$. Subtracting those tuples from $R$ leaves only tuples that belong to both $R$ and $S$, which is the set intersection $R \cap S$.

questions.stem: When mapping an EER specialization hierarchy using the Single Flat Table method, what major database constraint CANNOT be enforced on subclass-specific attributes?

options.B: Foreign key references pointing to external tables
options.C: NOT NULL constraints on subclass-specific attributes

questions.explanation: In a single flat table containing attributes of all subclasses, any row belonging to subclass A must store NULL for attributes belonging to subclass B. Therefore, subclass-specific attributes cannot enforce `NOT NULL`.

questions.stem: In ER modeling, under what condition can a binary relationship set be completely eliminated by collapsing it into an entity relation without creating redundant or null data?

options.A: When the relationship is One-to-One and both participating entity sets have Total Participation
options.B: When the relationship is Many-to-Many with descriptive attributes
options.C: When both entity sets are weak entity sets
options.D: When the relationship has partial participation on both sides

questions.explanation: When a 1:1 relationship has total participation on both participating entity sets, every entity in A matches exactly one in B and vice versa. Merging them into a single table introduces zero nulls and zero redundancy.

questions.stem: Why does executing an UPDATE statement on an SQL view defined with a JOIN across two base tables fail to guarantee deterministic execution?

options.A: Because relational storage managers do not support index lookups on views
options.B: Because the query optimizer cannot generate execution trees for views
options.C: Because the SQL standard limits view definitions to a maximum of 256 characters
options.D: Because an update on a join view can lead to ambiguous side-effects on base tables, potentially modifying unintended parent tuples or violating foreign keys

questions.explanation: Updating a join view can cause unpredictable side effects—such as updating shared parent attributes across multiple child rows or creating orphaned records—making unambiguous translation to base tables impossible.
